message.content:
You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-cmds):
- file: driver/elf_syms.cpp:215
- category: duplication
- title: fn_range duplicates symbolize's covering-FUNC-symbol scan
- detail: symbolize (elf_syms.cpp:159-213) and fn_range (215-246) both walk every SHT_SYMTAB section and run the identical candidate-selection predicate (SHN_UNDEF skip, STT_FUNC only, st_value <= addr, size-covered-or-preceding-label, best_value monotonic) -- lines 186-193 and 231-237 are byte-for-byte the same logic, ~30 duplicated lines. The only differences: symbolize also resolves the name through str_sh (and REJECTS a candidate whose name offset is out of bounds/unterminated, lines 195-199), while fn_range never loads str_sh at all and keeps size. Extract one static helper (e.g. find_covering_func(buf, eh, addr, need_name) -> {value, size, name}) used by both.
- claimed safety: Behavior-preserving only if the helper gates the string-table lookup and the bad-name rejection on need_name: symbolize skips unnamed/corrupt-name candidates and skips symtabs with an invalid sh_link, fn_range accepts them -- the helper must keep that divergence (a need_name flag does it exactly). With that, both functions' outputs are bit-identical on every input, including malformed ELFs.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. input.description: Find all references to fn_range and symbolize across repos

input.reason: Verified by reading driver/elf_syms.cpp in full. symbolize (172-205) and fn_range (225-242) duplicate the section walk plus an identical 5-condition covering-FUNC predicate (lines 187-193 vs 232-237, same modulo one comment). The claim's safety analysis is exactly right and complete: the only two behavioral divergences are (1) symbolize skips a whole symtab with invalid sh_link/unloadable str_sh header (178-182) while fn_range never loads str_sh, and (2) symbolize rejects out-of-bounds/unterminated-name candidates (195-199) BEFORE updating best_value/found, so corrupt-name symbols do not advance the monotonic bar, while fn_range accepts them and does. A need_name flag gating both the per-section str_sh handling and the per-candidate name rejection reproduces each function bit-identically, including on malformed ELFs. No hidden third divergence exists (identical prologue, loop bounds, break semantics; fn_range's extra st_size tracking is covered by a {value,size,name} return that symbolize ignores). Callers (driver/cmd_profile.cpp:200-204) use only the public signatures, driver/elf_syms_test.cpp has no symbolize/fn_range tests pinning internals, and no references exist in andesim-demo or vsim_andesim. Only nit: the duplicated span is ~25 lines, not ~30, and "byte-for-byte" ignores the comment on line 191.
